limits: The live observations of this page are single requests made on 2026-10-12 through the build machine's proxy with openpyxl 3.1.5, requests 2.34.2, beautifulsoup4 4.15.0, Python 3.14.6, plus runs of the chapter's projects on the real files of the online materials; web sites change and nothing re-checks them.

openpyxl's newest stable release on PyPI on 2026-10-12 was 3.1.5, uploaded 2024-06-28 (Requires-Python >=3.8, licence MIT); its documentation front page names 3.1.3, generated May 29, 2024. The page's examples were recorded under openpyxl 3.1.5.

One openpyxl program printed the same under each of the seven 3.14 releases, 3.13, 3.12 and the page's own runtime, Pyodide 0.28.2 (CPython 3.13.2) (the releases recorded 2026-10-12 with each interpreter installed by uv, every warning an error; bodies equal: True).
The programs that need openpyxl were run on the build machine under Python 3.14.6 (32 recorded runs in third_party_record_v1_0_0.json) with workbooks built in a temporary folder.

The page's in-browser Python is Pyodide's CPython 3.13, whose package list has no openpyxl, so the page carries 2 wheels of its own, downloaded from PyPI and checked by SHA-256 (openpyxl 3.1.5 (sha256 5282c12b107b...), et_xmlfile 2.0.0 (sha256 7a91720bc756...); both MIT licence; et_xmlfile also ships the Python licence for code derived from the standard library), and installs them into the browser Python when it starts; the comparison of every example's output with the stored output, recorded in that same Python (Pyodide 0.28.2, CPython 3.13.2), are part of the page test.

Every stored input-output example of the chapter was re-run in the page's own browser Python (Pyodide, CPython 3.13) by the page test and compared with the value recorded in that same Python (Pyodide 0.28.2, CPython 3.13.2, with the page's two wheels); two stored values differ from those a Python 3.14.6 run gave: Cached value loss gives (500, None), because the 3.13 library writes the empty value element in the form the example's replacement expects, and Hiding rows columns shows the column element with a space before the closing slash; the one example that started a second interpreter with subprocess (import census2010) cannot run in a browser, so research version 1.0.2 changed it to import in the same process and the starting of a real interpreter stays recorded in the document's executed behaviours.

Not executed in the build environment: Microsoft Excel itself (no copy was available, so what Excel draws and what it does with a file are taken from the chapter, the documentation and the files Excel saved), Google Sheets, pandas, a Windows machine, the Ecma and ISO pages of the file format standard (the first reset the connection, the second answered 403; the Library of Congress description of the format was read instead), and the figures of the chapter other than 14-6, 14-7, 14-10 and 14-11.
